connectorUiConfig.title: Cloudflare CCF via Blob Storage
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: The Cloudflare data connector provides the capability to ingest Cloudflare logs into Microsoft Sentinel using the Cloudflare Logpush and Azure Blob Storage. Refer to [Cloudflare documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/about/) for more information.

resourceProvider.permissionsDisplayText: Read and Write permissions are required.

customs.name: Storage Account Resource Group permissions
customs.description: The identity running the deployment needs the following Azure roles on the Storage Account resource group: **Owner**, or a combination **Contributor** + **User Access Administrator**

customs.name: Storage Account permissions
customs.description: The identity running the deployment needs the following Azure roles on the Storage Account: **Storage Blob Data Reader** role and **Storage Queue Data Contributor**

customs.name: Cloudflare permissions
customs.description: Ensure Log Share permissions are enabled, before attempting to read or configure a Logpush job. For more information refer to the [Roles](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/permissions/#roles) section.

customs.name: Role assignment propagation
customs.description: Newly granted Azure role assignments (Storage Blob Data Reader, Storage Queue Data Contributor) can take up to 5 minutes to propagate. If the initial connection check fails with `BLB40011` ("Access to the queue was denied"), wait ~5 minutes and click **Connect** again.

instructionSteps.title: 1. Create a storage account and a blob container
instructionSteps.description: Before setting up logpush in Cloudflare, first create a storage account and a blob container in  Azure. Follow the steps in the [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-create?tabs=azure-portal) to create an Azure Storage account.

instructionSteps.title: 2. Generate a Blob SAS URL
instructionSteps.description: Before setting up logpush in Cloudflare, generate a Blob SAS URL for your storage account container. Follow the steps in the [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-services/document-intelligence/authentication/create-sas-tokens?view=doc-intel-4.0.0&tabs=azure-portal#generating-sas-tokens) to create a Blob SAS URL with **Write** and **List** permissions for the blob container you created in the previous step.

instructionSteps.title: 3. Collecting logs from Cloudflare to your Blob container
instructionSteps.description: Follow the steps in the [documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/get-started/enable-destinations/azure/) for collecting logs from Cloudflare to your Blob container.

instructionSteps.title: 4. Connect Cloudflare Logs to Microsoft Sentinel
instructionSteps.description: To enable Cloudflare logs for Microsoft Sentinel, click **Add new collector**, fill in the required fields (including granting the Microsoft Sentinel service principal **Storage Blob Data Reader** on the target storage account), and click **Connect**.

parameters.label: Cloudflare account name
parameters.description: A short, lowercase identifier for this Cloudflare account (letters, digits and hyphens). Used as a prefix when naming the DCR, DCE, data connector and storage queues created for this account.
parameters.name: CloudflareAccountName

parameters.label: Storage account name
parameters.description: The name of the Azure Storage account that receives Cloudflare Logpush data.
parameters.name: StorageAccountName

parameters.label: Blob container name
parameters.description: The blob container inside the storage account where Cloudflare Logpush writes log files.
parameters.name: ContainerName

parameters.label: The event grid topic name of the blob container's storage account if exist. else keep empty.
parameters.description: Azure Event Grid allows only one system topic per storage account. If a previous Cloudflare collector already created a system topic for this storage account, paste its name here (e.g. 'sentinel-cloudflare-<storage-account-name>') so this deployment reuses it and only adds a new event subscription. To find it, open the storage account in the Azure portal and go to 'Events'. Leave this empty only when deploying the first collector against this storage account.
parameters.name: EGSystemTopicName

parameters.label: Custom table name (optional)
parameters.description: The custom table this collector writes to. Must end with '_CL'. Leave as the default 'CloudflareV2_CL' to use the built-in table that the solution's parsers, workbooks, hunting queries and analytics rules query. Enter a different name only to isolate this collector's data in its own table; that custom table is created automatically but is NOT consumed by the solution's content.
parameters.name: TableName
